title: Form 7 — Objection to Inclusion / Claim for Deletion
summary: Form 7 is used to object to a name being included in the electoral roll, or to seek deletion of an entry — for example after the elector's death, a duplicate registration, or a person no longer ordinarily resident at the registered address.
body:
Use Form 7 when you need to flag that an entry in the electoral roll should not be there: the elector has died, has moved away permanently, is registered in more than one place (duplicate), or was never actually eligible/resident there. Any registered elector within the same constituency can file an objection. Filing a large number of objections (the Election Commission has noted more than five by one individual) can trigger a mandatory review by the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) to check the objections are genuine and not used to harass or intimidate other electors.

Form 7 is not for correcting your own entry (that is Form 8) and not for new registration (that is Form 6).
caution: Because Form 7 can be misused to challenge genuine electors, VoteAssist must present it neutrally and warn users that objections require evidence and are reviewed by the ERO — never suggest using it to target specific communities or individuals.
